owner_bench_points_2026_11_21.source: Owner, in chat on 2026-11-21 (paraphrased on the pages, first person where it is his observation; no numbers given or printed)
owner_bench_points_2026_11_21.phone-wont-turn-on-after-drop: Depends on the drop and what 'completely dead' means. No signs of life at all generally means board damage; sometimes a peripheral (battery, charging assembly); sometimes a phone that appears dead only needs a screen.
owner_bench_points_2026_11_21.phone-touch-screen-not-working-after-dro: Dead touch after a drop is generally the whole display. Connectors rarely pop loose now (covers, shields, clips); possible if a previous repair left a cover off; board unlikely but possible. Dead zones can come back intermittently but never fix themselves permanently.
owner_bench_points_2026_11_21.black-spot-on-phone-screen: Ink blots are often slow to spread, can stay unchanged a long time or migrate fast; on phones he sees, usually slow. A damaged display can still fail entirely at any moment. Two bench photos supplied and added (Galaxy ink blot; iPhone with a small blot and the area below failed to white). iPhone photo cropped to remove a customer's banking app icons; EXIF stripped from both.
owner_bench_points_2026_11_21.cracked-iphone-camera-lens: Tape over cracked camera glass to protect the inner lens; its coating is delicate, debris on it effectively cannot be cleaned and touching it makes it worse, so a cracked cover can mean a new camera module too. A camera not working after a drop is usually a dead or internally damaged module, not a loose connector. Glass-only replacement on recent iPhones: owner believes yes and asked for a fact check; Apple's iPhone 16 and 17 repair manuals list only Back Glass and Camera procedures, so the page says shops can often do it and that Apple doesn't list it as a separate part.
owner_bench_points_2026_11_21.ps5 guides: Owner: 'just use the official advice, it's not my area.' PS5 pages follow Sony only; their bench-note questions were removed.
